text:
Recent work supports separating recommendation acceptance from explanation quality and general relevance. A [2026 movie study](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/ICWSM/article/view/42667) measured intention to watch alongside perceptions; contextualized explanations improved intentions, with effects depending on preferences and engagement. [Fleisig et al. (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.126/) argue that annotator disagreement can contain meaningful perspectives rather than simply errors. Practical synthesis: annotate each user–item response on separate dimensions—explicit choice now, general interest, explicit rejection with stated reasons, and uncertainty about item identity. Preserve the original wording and distinguish missing evidence from negative feedback. Compatibility, ownership and mood remain unknown unless reported; title/description overlap supports a textual connection, not a suitability claim.

For auditable evidence, link each annotation to user ID, exact item ID, displayed position, full-catalog unseen-item rank, catalog size and model version. This is a proposed audit design, not a validated metric from the cited studies. Use a written codebook, independently double-code the small feedback set, preserve original labels, and document adjudication. Measure agreement between coders interpreting the same response—not between users with different preferences. Report label counts, raw agreement, a suitable chance-corrected coefficient and uncertainty intervals; a [2024 annotation-quality review](https://aclanthology.org/2024.cl-3.1.pdf) emphasizes sample-size justification, confidence intervals and transparent reporting. With twenty users, summarize patterns by user/category and retain ambiguous cases; repeated item judgments do not create additional independent users. Treat qualitative findings as exploratory diagnostics, separately from the pinned validation HR@10.
